title: Government Page Navigation Hierarchy
description: Complete official page chrome: skip link, banner, header with nav, breadcrumb, section navigation, footer, and identifier — in canonical DOM order.

components.reason: Must be the first focusable element in body; targets the main content region
Official government website banner; always the first visible element
Site header; navbar and search live inside it (use navbar/default.html and search/small.html as children)
Place below header, above the page h1, when the site is more than two levels deep
Sidebar nav for section-heavy pages; place in a column beside main content
Table of contents for long articles; links must match heading ids
Site footer; last major element in body
Official agency identifier; directly below the footer

nesting: Canonical DOM order is 1→2→3→(content: 4, 5, 6)→7→8. Component 1 targets the main region. Navbar (navbar/default.html) and search (search/small.html) are children of component 3. Components 4-6 are content-level and mutually optional
validationOrder: Skip-nav target id exists on the main content region
Banner is the first visible element; identifier is the last
Side-navigation current item has class usa-current and aria-current='page'
a11yNotes: Never remove the skip link — it is the first tab stop
Landmarks: banner, header (role omitted, it is implicit), nav elements each need a distinct aria-label when multiple navs exist
Identifier links to the agency's official site
Keep heading hierarchy h1 (page title) → h2 sections below the breadcrumb
agentPromptSequence: 1. Place skip-nav as the first element in body
2. Add banner, then header (nest navbar/search inside as needed)
3. Add breadcrumb below header when depth warrants it
4. Choose side-navigation (sections) or in-page-navigation (long article) — rarely both
